title: Extend Introduction Mechanism With Interactions
description: Extend the introduction (tour) mechanism so a step can require completing a list of interactions (sometimes ordered, sometimes not), not just a single advance condition. Replace the single `IntroductionAdvance` (next/action/utility/tool/panel/expand) contract with `interactions: Vec<IntroductionInteraction>` + `ordered: bool` on `IntroductionStepDefinition` (framework/core/rs/lib.rs), adding new camera-navigation interaction kinds (pan/zoom/orbit) for 3D windows. Add a pure gesture classifier in infinite/world/r3f (diff before/after camera snapshots on OrbitControls start/end to detect pan vs zoom vs orbit). Wire completion through the React shell (framework/renderer/react/index.tsx): new completed-interactions state, a shared completeIntroductionInteraction() path (celebrates via existing celebrateElements/data-celebrated ring, auto-advances when all complete), gesture intercept via onAction, World3dHost wiring. Add a checklist UI to UIIntroduction (ui/js/react/index.tsx) showing each interaction with a checkmark (and order number when ordered). Update Rust consumers (framework/plugin validation, puzzle/plugin reference tour, framework/renderer/wgpu chrome tour) and rewrite the aggregator's introduction steps in mit-bestand/aggregator/brand.ts — step "viewport" becomes an unordered 3-item checklist (zoom, pan, orbit) on the puzzle3d-main window. No backwards compatibility; extend existing test suites, no new test files. Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/extend-the-introduction-mechanism-steady-river.md.
summary:
Follow-up fix: the celebration for a completed pan/zoom/orbit interaction was celebrating every open pane of the same window kind, not just the pane the user actually gestured on. Root cause: `completeIntroductionInteraction`/`advanceIntroductionByDoing` fell back to `interaction.celebrate ?? step.introduce`, a window-KIND-level element id (e.g. "framework.window.puzzle3dMain") that `elementIdSelector` matches via `data-element-alias` on every open pane of that kind (e.g. both "puzzle3d-main-top" and "puzzle3d-main-perspective" in a split view) — not just the one that performed the gesture.

Fix (framework/renderer/react/index.tsx): both functions now accept an optional `celebrateOverride` parameter that takes precedence over the interaction/step-level celebrate id. The camera-gesture intercept in `onAction` (the `NOTE_WORLD_NAVIGATION_ACTION_ID` handler) passes `windowElementId(windowId)` — the reporting pane's own unique per-instance element id, not the shared kind alias — as this override, for both the per-interaction celebration and the final step-complete celebration (threaded through when the gesture also completes the last interaction). Non-gesture interaction kinds (action/utility/tool/panel/expand) are unaffected — they never pass an override, so they keep celebrating `interaction.celebrate ?? step.introduce` as before, which was never ambiguous for them (those target a single UI element, not a window kind with potentially multiple open panes).

Added a regression test in ui/js/react/index.tsx (celebrateElements describe block) that renders two panes sharing a window-kind `data-element-alias` and asserts: celebrating by the kind alias stamps both panes (the bug), while celebrating by one pane's own element id stamps only that pane (the fix). Verified: ui-react and framework-renderer-react vitest suites both green (only the same pre-existing unrelated failures in tree helpers/CanvasPickMenu/UnifiedGumball, untouched by this change).
